title: Which Reading a Booked Stretch Is Measured From
content:
The miles a reading the marketplace books takes off the interval are not counted before a completed inspection dated within seven calendar days of the handling date stands on the vehicle's condition record.

Which reading the booked stretch on a Keyturn Vehicle Listing is anchored to is read off the condition record.

1. Where a completed inspection dated within 7 calendar days of the handling date stands on the vehicle's condition record, the anchor reading is the highest reading standing on that vehicle's odometer records.

2. Where no such inspection stands but an odometer record dated within 30 calendar days of the handling date does, the anchor reading is the reading that most recent odometer record carries.

3. Otherwise the anchor reading is the odometer standing on the listing.

### Points of judgement

*Highest on the first clause, most recent on the second.* Where a completed inspection stands inside 7 calendar days, the anchor is the highest reading standing on the vehicle's odometer records, whenever it was taken. Where the second clause is reached instead, the anchor is the reading carried by the most recent odometer record, even where an earlier record carries a higher one.

*At each day boundary.* A completed inspection dated exactly 7 calendar days before the handling date is within the window and puts the vehicle on the first clause; one dated 8 calendar days before it does not. An odometer record dated exactly 30 calendar days before the handling date is within its window; one dated 31 calendar days before it is not.

*A vehicle with neither.* Where no completed inspection stands within 7 calendar days and no odometer record within 30, the third clause governs.
